title: Letter 36 — God Is Our Refuge and Strength
attribution_note: Letter 36 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The continual change of this life

pairs.en: I received a letter from you, from which I learned the sorrow and bitterness of your soul. What is to be done? Life in this world is not without this. In the air it is now dark, now clear, now stormy, now still; so also on the sea: now a calm, now waves; so also in us there is no changeless state: now we rejoice, now we grieve, now we fear, now we hope; such is the life of this world. This continual change teaches us how we ought to bear ourselves in happiness and unhappiness, in joy and in sorrow. Joy has come — expect sorrow also; we fall into sorrow — then expect gladness also.

But blessed is he who can govern the ship of his soul in time of storm and foul weather. For this one must care — but effort without help from above is powerless; therefore one must ask this of God, the Governor of all. *“God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble”* [Psalm 45:2]. So faith emboldens itself in times of sorrowful happenings, and defends itself, as with a shield, against the fiery darts of the enemy, by hope in the Most High.

He is *“the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off upon the sea”* [Psalm 64:6]. He is the same both for me, the poor one, and for you: *“the eyes of all wait upon Thee”* [Psalm 144:15], and I in my sorrows lift up my tearful eyes to Him. To all He is Helper and Defender — so also to me, and to you. He looks not upon faces, but upon our heart and faith (cf. Deuteronomy 10:17; 1 Samuel 16:7). As the sun enlightens and comforts all who look upon it with its brightest appearance, so the eternal and unsetting Sun is enlightenment and comfort to all who look upon Him by faith. Of this the prophet says: *“Unto Thee lift I up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in the heavens.* *Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress; so our eyes wait upon the Lord our God, until that He have mercy upon us”* [Psalm 122:1–2].
Commending myself and you to God's mercy, I remain
Your well-wisher, Tikhon of Zadonsk.
